The physical dyadic Ising spectrum realizes all M roots. The proof distinguishes unconditional causal-break maps from conditioned postselection. value.rationale: The recent physical paper demonstrates that three pairwise reduced channels can be completely incoherent while a multi-time process retains coherence. It is natural to ask how many such observation times a fixed finite memory can conceal, what exact memory preparation and spectrum enable saturation, how imbalance prevents it, and how much process coherence remains. The theorem answers all four, yields a sharp ensemble-purity penalty usable as a finite-memory diagnostic, and provides an explicit optimal dyadic-Ising implementation with residual coherence of order N ln2. The result goes beyond a numerical small-instance census; the phase-ensemble entropy itself is acknowledged as known in other mathematics.
